note.text: This practical uses a simplified classroom record, not an actual share issue. Start by labelling authorised and issued share counts, nominal value, the call per share and unpaid calls. Multiply a share count by a per-share amount to obtain capital in CFA francs. Called but unpaid is arrears; issued but not yet called is uncalled. Unissued shares are neither called nor paid-up capital. A diagram of gaps or a table can help keep these distinctions visible.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to calculate authorised, issued, called, paid-up and uncalled amounts from a labelled fictional record. Builds on: the company-capital distinctions just learned. Leads to: judging financing constraints and later growth plans.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: Record these model columns in an exercise book: share count, nominal value, amount called and amount received. For issued shares, split nominal capital into called and uncalled; split called into paid-up and arrears. The same money must not be added twice. The displayed table matches the worked example and helps check the stages before independent questions.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Check units and identities: issued = called + uncalled; called = paid-up + arrears. Authorised minus issued is the unissued ceiling. These equalities concern the stated instalment model; they are not a balance-sheet total including debt or profit reserves. Correct a heading error before doing arithmetic.

key_words.meaning: issued share count multiplied by nominal value
called share contributions not yet received
the unrequested nominal amount on already issued shares
checking that component amounts sum to the stated total

mistake.wrong: Issued capital is always the number of shares without a currency unit.
mistake.right: nominal issue: issued share count multiplied by nominal value.
mistake.why: Multiplying by currency per share produces a capital amount.

worked_example.problem: A classroom record has {80} authorised shares, {50} issued shares, nominal value {1000}, a call of {600} per share and arrears of {2000} CFA francs. Reconcile the stages.

cards.idea: Distinguish these features before judging a business.
example: nominal issue: issued share count multiplied by nominal value.
arrears: called share contributions not yet received.
uncalled capital: the unrequested nominal amount on already issued shares.
reconciliation: checking that component amounts sum to the stated total.

questions.prompt: Textbook model: {authorised} shares are authorised at nominal {nominal} CFA francs each. What is authorised nominal capital?

misconceptions.explain: That is the smaller issued amount, not the authorisation ceiling.
That is a number of shares, not a currency capital amount.

solution: Multiply the authorised ceiling count by nominal value.

questions.prompt: Textbook model: {issued} of {authorised} authorised shares are issued at nominal {nominal} CFA francs each. Find nominal issued capital.

misconceptions.explain: That is authorised capital, including unissued shares.
Called capital uses the requested instalment, not the full nominal issued amount.

questions.prompt: Textbook model: {issued} shares are issued; the call is {called} CFA francs per share. Find called capital.

misconceptions.explain: That is the full nominal issue, not the amount called.
Paid-up subtracts unpaid calls, which is a later step.

solution: Use issued shares multiplied by the call per share.

questions.prompt: Textbook model: called capital is {calledTotal} CFA francs, including unpaid calls of {arrears}. Calculate paid-up capital.

misconceptions.explain: Unpaid calls are not receipts; subtract them.

solution: Subtract the called amount that has not been received.

questions.prompt: Textbook model: {issued} shares have nominal value {nominal} CFA francs each, but only {called} per share has been called. Calculate uncalled capital on those issued shares.

misconceptions.explain: That is unissued authorised capital, a different gap.
Arrears are called but unpaid; uncalled has not yet been requested.
